name: City Centre and UD Town
tagline: Around the station, with the night market and the malls
description: The commercial core around the railway station, where UD Town's open-air food and shopping complex functions as the city's main evening gathering place, with the night market, the malls and the bus connections all close by. Everything practical in Udon Thani is inside this area.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the night markets, the malls and the train all on foot
pros: UD Town and the night markets a short walk away
Station, buses and every service nearby
Best internet and the most rental supply
cons: Traffic and noise through the day
The highest rents in the city, though still low

name: Nong Prajak
tagline: Around the city park, where Udon Thani exercises
description: The district surrounding Nong Prajak, a large lake and park with running paths, outdoor gyms and food stalls that fills every evening. The streets around it hold cafes, guesthouses and some of the more pleasant apartments in the city, all within walking distance of the centre.
bestFor: Stays where a run or a walk round the lake at sunset is the daily routine
pros: The park, its running paths and evening food stalls
Cafes and quieter streets around the water
Ten to fifteen minutes on foot to the centre
cons: Rents slightly above the outer districts
Busy with exercisers and stalls in the evening

name: Ban Chiang Road and the Expat Strip
tagline: Where the long-term foreign residents ended up
description: The streets west of the centre where the bars, restaurants and services aimed at Udon Thani's substantial foreign resident population have concentrated over the years. It is not to everyone's taste, but it is where English is most reliably spoken and where the community is easiest to find.
bestFor: Arrivals who want an English-speaking landing pad and an existing community
pros: The most English spoken anywhere in the city
cons: The bar scene here is specific and not for everyone

name: Mueang Outer Ring
tagline: Suburban housing estates, houses and space for very little
description: The residential areas spreading out along the ring road, where modern Thai housing estates offer whole houses with gardens and parking for less than a small apartment costs in Bangkok. A motorbike or car is necessary, and the everyday shopping is at the big-box stores on the ring.
bestFor: Long stays wanting a whole house and willing to ride into town
pros: Whole houses with gardens at very low rents
Big supermarkets and hardware stores on the ring road
cons: A motorbike or car is essential
Fifteen to twenty minutes into the centre

name: Ban Chiang Village (48 km east)
tagline: The Bronze Age site 48 km east of the city
description: A village 48 kilometres east of the city holding the UNESCO-listed Ban Chiang archaeological site, where excavations uncovered a Bronze Age culture and its distinctive painted pottery. It is rural, very quiet and cheap, with the site museum and a small guesthouse trade the only activity.
bestFor: A short rural stay built around the site rather than the city
pros: The UNESCO site and its museum on the doorstep
The lowest costs anywhere in the province
cons: Almost no services and very slow internet
Essentially nothing to do beyond the site
